name: Hindu dharma rubric (deed, word and thought)
basis: Sanatana dharma as taught in the Bhagavad Gita, Mahabharata, Upanishads, Puranas and the ten marks of dharma (Manusmriti 6.92). Karma is of the body (deeds), speech and mind (thoughts and intentions: Manusmriti 12.5-7, Gita 17.14-16).

scale.note: points are a positive integer 1-50 computed by the app, not chosen by the model; the sign comes from the principle (punya = +, paap = -). Points = principle range scaled by the factors, then by the mode multiplier.

factors: Magnitude: how large, costly or severe the act is.
Reach: how many beings are affected and how vulnerable they are.
Intent: how deliberate and sincere; for show or reward is low, accidental harm is very low; for a thought, a passing flash is low and dwelling on it is high.
Consistency: a one-off, occasional, or a steady habit.
Amends (paap only): sincere regret or repair lowers the points a little, never to zero.

categories.seva: Selfless service to people, community, elders, the needy.
categories.family_duty: Care, time and responsibility toward family, parents and elders.
categories.jeev_daya: Compassion to living beings (cows, animals, birds, insects, people in distress).
categories.satya: Truthful speech and conduct; lying, deceit, false promises.
categories.vani: Kind versus harsh speech: gossip, insult, slander, comforting words.
categories.krodh: Anger: handling it with patience (punya) or acting on it (paap).
categories.honesty_work: Honesty and diligence at work or study; cheating, theft, bribery.
categories.daan: Charity and generosity; greed or hoarding at others' cost.
categories.gratitude_bhakti: Prayer, japa, scripture study, satsang, gratitude, devotion.
categories.ahimsa_food: Non-violence in deed and diet; harm to living beings.

principles.label: Paropakāra
principles.source: Vyasa on the Puranas: paropakāraḥ puṇyāya, pāpāya parapīḍanam
principles.about: Helping others without selfish motive.

principles.label: Annadāna
principles.about: Giving food to the hungry.

principles.label: Dāna
principles.about: Giving money, goods or time according to one's means.

principles.label: Go-seva, Jīva-dayā
principles.source: Puranic tradition of go-seva and compassion to beings
principles.about: Caring for cows, animals, birds and all living beings.

principles.label: Mātṛ-Pitṛ seva
principles.about: Serving and honouring parents, elders and teachers.

principles.label: Atithi seva
principles.about: Welcoming and feeding a guest or stranger.

principles.label: Satya
principles.about: Speaking and keeping the truth, especially at a personal cost.

principles.label: Kṣamā, Akrodha
principles.about: Forgiving, and staying calm when provoked.

principles.label: Dama, Śauca
principles.about: Self-control, restraint and purity of body and mind.

principles.label: Bhakti, Sādhanā
principles.about: Worship, japa, scripture study, satsang, meditation, gratitude.

principles.label: Svadharma
principles.about: Doing one's own duty honestly (work, study, household).

principles.label: Vidyā-dāna
principles.about: Teaching or sharing knowledge.

principles.label: Ahiṁsā
principles.about: Non-violence in deed, word, thought and diet; protecting someone from harm.

principles.label: Hiṁsā
principles.about: Physical violence, killing, serious cruelty.

principles.label: Para-pīḍā
principles.source: Vyasa on the Puranas: pāpāya parapīḍanam
principles.about: Deliberately causing pain or distress to others.

principles.label: Asatya
principles.about: Lying, deceit, breaking a promise.

principles.label: Steya
principles.about: Stealing, bribery, cheating.

principles.label: Krodha
principles.about: Acting on anger.

principles.label: Paruṣa-vāṇī
principles.about: Harsh speech, insult, gossip, slander.

principles.label: Lobha, Ahaṅkāra
principles.about: Greed, pride, envy, showing off.

principles.label: Pramāda, Vyasana
principles.about: Laziness, addiction, neglect of duty.

principles.label: Mātṛ-Pitṛ anādara
principles.about: Neglecting, insulting or abandoning parents and elders.

principles.label: Sevā-upekṣā
principles.about: Refusing help to someone in genuine need when able to give it.

principles.label: Maitrī, Karuṇā
principles.source: Bhagavad Gita 12.13 (adveṣṭā sarva-bhūtānāṁ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca)
principles.about: Goodwill, compassion and well-wishing toward others held in the mind.

principles.label: Manaḥ-prasāda
principles.about: Serenity, gentleness and purity of mind; letting go of resentment.

principles.label: Śubha-saṅkalpa
principles.source: Shiva Sankalpa Sukta, Shukla Yajurveda 34.1 (tan me manaḥ śiva-saṅkalpam astu)
principles.about: A good resolve, an intention to do right, or gratitude held in the heart.

principles.label: Paścāttāpa
principles.source: Manusmriti 11.228 (sincere regret frees one from the wrong)
principles.about: Honest regret for a wrong done, with the wish to set it right.

principles.label: Dveṣa, Īrṣyā
principles.about: Envy, hatred and ill will toward others in the mind.

principles.label: Abhidhyā
principles.about: Coveting what belongs to others; craving far more than one needs.

principles.label: Aśubha-saṅkalpa
principles.about: Wishing harm, plotting revenge or dwelling on hurting someone.

rules: Score only the person's own deeds, words, thoughts and intentions. Never what others did to them. Imagined, hypothetical or quoted things are not scored.
Omit ordinary neutral activity (commuting, meals, routine work, chores).
A deed that followed a thought is one item (the deed). Resisting a temptation is mode refrained and the urge is not scored.
Split separate deeds in one sentence into separate items; merge near-duplicates. Rate honestly; do not give every item the same ratings.
Refer to principles only by id. Never claim a verse number.
If the text mentions self-harm, suicide, abuse, or intent to harm others, set safety_flag true and return no actions.

scoring.formula: score = 0.40*magnitude/4 + 0.25*reach/4 + 0.25*intent/4 + 0.10*consistency/2 (0..1). For paap: score *= 0.4 + 0.6*min(1, intent/2) (accidental harm is light) and score *= 1 - 0.15*amends. points = round((low + (high - low) * score) * mode multiplier), kept inside 1..high of the principle.

done.about: The person actually did it: a deed, or words actually spoken.

refrained.about: The person felt the pull to do wrong and held back. Counted as merit (restraint). The urge itself is not counted as paap.

regret.about: Sincere regret or repentance for something wrong already done (pashchattapa). Small merit; the wrong itself is scored separately.

intended.about: A resolve, plan or wish to act that has not happened yet ("I will", "I want to", "I should").

thought.about: Only a thought or feeling in the mind, not acted on. Good thoughts (goodwill, compassion, gratitude, calm) earn small merit; harmful ones (envy, hatred, greed, plotting harm) are small paap.
